cards.explanation: The answer is Rabbah of the Ammonites. God says, “Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into fortified Jerusalem.” Rabbah is the Ammonites' city, sitting at the end of the second road. Two roads, one starting land, and a signpost at the branch. Ezekiel, the prophet, is basically drawing a map with a sword on it.

The answer is an omen. Verse 21 says the king of Babylon stands at the fork “…to seek an omen…” and then lists the arrows, the idols and the liver. That's a whole lot of effort at one fork in the road, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 22 says, “In his right hand appears the portent for Jerusalem…” The omen points to Jerusalem, and Rabbah isn't what shows up in his hand. It's a sneaky little detail, friends.

The answer is battering rams. The king is “…to direct the battering rams against the gates…” The same verse lists a ramp and a siege wall too. It's a heavy list, so I'll just say the gates are the target.

The answer is guilt. The omen “…will draw attention to their guilt and take them captive.” To those who swore allegiance to the king, it will seem like a false omen. I bet they brush it off, but the text says it draws attention to their guilt anyway.

The answer is True. The Lord GOD says the sins are revealed in all their deeds, and then, “…you shall be taken in hand.” It's a sober verse, and I think it's one to read slowly. The text says it plainly, so we can too.

The answer is final. God says to the profane and wicked prince of Israel, “…the day has come for your final punishment.” The verse doesn't soften it, because the day has already come. I think this is a heavy part, so let's take it slow, friends.

The answer is the turban and the crown. God says, “Remove the turban, and take off the crown.” Both of those go on the head, and God gives the order for them to come off. I wear a tall chef's hat, so I'd be nervous if someone told me to take mine off.
The answer is lowly. God says, “Exalt the lowly and bring low the exalted.” Two directions at once: one goes up and one goes down. And it comes right after “Things will not remain as they are…”

The answer is the arrival of the One it belongs to. God says it “…will not be restored until the arrival of Him to whom it belongs, to whom I have assigned the right of judgment.” The ruin waits for Him. I'll let that sit for a second, friends.

The answer is False. God tells Ezekiel to prophesy concerning the Ammonites and their contempt, saying, “A sword! A sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to consume, to flash like lightning…” The Ammonites are named in this word from God. This is a heavy word, and the text doesn't let them off.

The answer is in their land of origin. God says, “In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.” The sword is told to go back in its sheath, and then God says where He will judge them: right where they began. That's the text's own wording, friends.

The answer is that they will not be remembered. God ends the message with, “You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.” I think this is a hard one to hear. It's a sober way to end, and it's what the text says.
